full_judgment:
Moyeenul Islam Chowdhury J : This is a petitioner under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898 for quashing the judgment and Order dated 15-2-2012 passed by the Additional Sessions Judge, 3rd Court, Khulna in Criminal Revision No. 40 of 2012 dismissing the revision and thereby confirming the order dated 18-12-2011 passed by the Executive Magistrate, 'Ga Anchal, Khulna in MP Case No. 369 of 2012 (Dumuria) under section 144 of the said Code appointing the Officer-in-Charge of Dumuria Police Station as the receiver of the disputed property. 

 2. Mr Md Mamun Aleem, learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the 2nd Party-Petitioners, submits that indisputably the proceedings under section 144 of the Code of Criminal Procedure were not converted into one under section 145 of the Code and in that view of the matter, the appointment of the Officer-in-Charge of Dumuria Police Station as the receiver of the disputed property by the Executive Magistrate is ex-facie illegal and against this backdrop, the impugned judgment and order dated 15-2-2012 passed in Criminal Revision No. 40 of 2102 upholding the order dated 18-12-2011 passed by the Executive Magistrate is 'non est.' in the eye of law. 

 3. Mr Md Mamun Aleem further submits that the order of appointment of the receiver of the disputed property was made on 18-12-2011 and by this time more than two months have already elapsed and in this perspective, the provisions of sub-section (6) of section 144 of the Code of Criminal Procedure will come into play and by that reason, the order dated 18-12-2011 is necessarily a defunct order. 

 4. It is a settled proposition of Jaw that no receiver can be appointed of the disputed property unless the proceedings under section 144 of the Code of Criminal Procedure are converted into one under section 145 of the Code. On this point, we are at one with the learned Advocate Mr Md Mamun Aleem. As such, we hold that the order dated 18-12-2011 passed by the Executive Magistrate and the impugned judgment and order rendered by the Additional Session Judge in Criminal Revision No. 40 of 2012 are bad in law. 

 5. Furthermore, it is an admitted fact that more than two months have already elapsed since the making of the order dated 18-12-2011 by the Executive Magistrate. In this regard, the provisions of sub-section (6) of section 144 of the Code of Criminal Procedure may be quoted below verbatim:- 

 144(6)- No order under this section shall remain in force for more than two months from the making thereof; unless, in cases of danger to human life, health or safety, or a likelihood of a riot or an affray, the Government, by notification in the official Gazette, otherwise directs." 

 6. It does not transpire from the record that the Government by a notification in the official gazette otherwise directed in this instance in cases of danger to human life, health of safety, or a likelihood of a riot or an affray as contemplated by sub-section (6) of section 144 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. So our definite conclusion is this: the order dated 18-12-2011. passed by the Executive Magistrate has already run its course and exhausted itself rendering the same to be a defunct order at this point of time.
